Accountable obligation owner.value: Product Compliance owns the Art. 123 basic-document filing determination for every product change; escalation to Regulatory Counsel for the authorization-vs-notification call

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Insurance Business Act Art. 123 (prior authorization to amend the statement of business procedures, general policy conditions and statement of calculation methods), Art. 125 (notification categories), Art. 3(1) and Art. 315, re-read on e-Gov Houreiy Kensaku at determination time together with the current Ordinance for Enforcement Art. 71 list and the FSA Comprehensive Supervisory Guidelines for Insurance Companies II-4

In-scope processes.value: Product change intake through the pre-use filing determination gate: every change to the statement of business procedures (jigyou-houhousho), general policy conditions (futsuu-hoken-yakkan) and premium/policy-reserve calculation method statement (santei-houhousho), for all lines and specifically the Variable Annuity separate-account and minimum-guarantee provisions

In-scope systems.value: Basic-document register and filing determination log in the Internal Regulatory System; US-state parallel determinations recorded against SERFF Filing Rules captures

Compliance procedure documented.value: Basic-Document Change Determination Procedure JP-123: intake, decomposition into the three basic documents, Art. 123(1) authorization vs Art. 123(2)/Ordinance Art. 71 notification classification, competent-authority routing (FSA Insurance Business Division vs Kanto Local Finance Bureau), 90-day standard processing period back-off, log entry

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Chief Actuary; re-approved annually and on every FSA Supervisory Guidelines revision or Ordinance for Enforcement amendment touching Art. 71

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per filing - the determination must close before the product build freeze; the FSA standard processing period of 90 days for a basic-document amendment authorization sets the latest application date backed off the intended sales-start date, and notification-only items still require lodgement before use

Deadline reminders configured.value: Internal Regulatory System milestone alerts at T-150 / T-120 / T-90 business days to the intended sales-start date on every open determination, plus a weekly open-determination report to the Insurance Product Manager

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Determination worksheet, dated captures of the Art. 71 notification list and the state SERFF filing rules, actuarial confirmation and counsel sign-off retained 10 years from withdrawal of the affected basic-document provision

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any basic-document provision used in sale without a closed determination is logged as a compliance exception with root cause, self-report assessment under Art. 128 reporting powers, and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Counsel signs every 'notification only' and every 'no filing required' call, and every late-determination remediation, before the log row closes

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All basic-document provisions that changed in the quarter per the Internal Regulatory System version history, plus every product/rider whose sales-start date fell in the quarter, across the Japan entity and each US writing company

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance - any changed basic-document provision sold without a closed, pre-dated determination is a fail; any Art. 123(1) item mis-classified as notification-only is a fail regardless of outcome; one or more fails escalates to the Head of Compliance and the Compliance Committee

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per filing; the test runs quarterly over that quarter's changed-provision population with 100% coverage of Art. 123(1) authorization items and Variable Annuity minimum-guarantee changes

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have authored or approved any sampled determination and must not sit in Product Compliance

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly JP-123 determination test workpaper (population extract, reconciliation, sample, re-performance notes, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under Regulation REG-030

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Determination log export, the authorization applications and FSA authorization letters, and the notification receipts, assemblable as an FSA on-site inspection or Art. 128 report response within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Affairs Manager is the single channel to the FSA Insurance Business Division and the Local Finance Bureau; General Counsel clears any admission of an unauthorized basic-document change before it leaves the company

checklist.step: Take in the approved product change and open a determination record
actions: In the Internal Regulatory System open Change Intake and filter Status = 'Product Committee approved, determination pending'.

Create a determination record and copy across: product name, entity (Japan branch/subsidiary or US writing company), line of business, intended sales-start date, distribution channels, and whether the change touches in-force policies or new business only.
Ask the Insurance Product Manager in writing for the commercial driver and the hard date driver (campaign start, competitor response, statutory change) and paste the reply onto the record.
Attach the signed product committee minute and name the determination folder <entity>-<product>-<intended sales-start date>.
checklist.done: the determination record carries entity, product, sales-start date and channel list with the committee minute attached.

checklist.step: Decompose the change into the three statutory basic documents
actions: Open the current authorized basic-document set in the Internal Regulatory System and place each element of the change on its own worksheet row.

Tag each row to one of: statement of business procedures (jigyou-houhousho - insured scope, sales area, channel, underwriting limits), general policy conditions (futsuu-hoken-yakkan and any tokuyaku rider wording), statement of calculation methods (santei-houhousho - premium bases, policy reserve method, surrender values), or NON-BASIC (sales collateral, internal manuals).
For policy-condition rows record the clause number and the wording version id being superseded.
For Variable Annuity rows flag separately anything touching the separate account (tokubetsu kanjou) asset menu, the minimum guarantee (saitei hoshou) benefit design, or the guarantee charge.
Send the tagged worksheet to the Product / Filing Actuary and ask for written confirmation that no calculation-method element has been missed.
checklist.done: every element of the change sits on a row tagged to one of the three basic documents or explicitly to NON-BASIC, with actuarial confirmation on file.

checklist.step: Classify each row as Art. 123(1) authorization, Art. 123(2) notification or out of scope
actions: Open the current Ordinance for Enforcement of the Insurance Business Act Art. 71 on e-Gov and read the enumerated categories for which prior notification replaces authorization.
Set each worksheet row to AUTHORIZATION (Art. 123(1)), NOTIFICATION (Art. 123(2) via Ordinance Art. 71) or OUT OF SCOPE, and paste the exact enumerated item number you relied on into the row.
Treat any change to premium rates, policy reserve method, guarantee design or the scope of insureds as AUTHORIZATION unless a named Art. 71 item plainly covers it.
Print the Art. 71 text you read to PDF, name it JP-ordinance-art71-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf and file it in the determination folder as the evidence behind the classification.
Highlight every AUTHORIZATION row - those set the critical path and carry the Art. 315 penalty exposure if used before approval.
checklist.done: every row shows AUTHORIZATION / NOTIFICATION / OUT OF SCOPE with the enumerated Art. 71 item quoted and a dated capture of the source text.

checklist.step: Read the FSA Supervisory Guidelines treatment for the affected provision type
actions: Open the FSA Comprehensive Supervisory Guidelines for Insurance Companies, Part II-4 (basic documents and product review) on the FSA website and read the review viewpoints for the affected provision type.
For Variable Annuity guarantee changes also read the guidelines on separate-account products and on the sales-suitability conditions the FSA attaches to authorization.
Record on the worksheet any guideline point that will require a supporting explanation in the application (rationale for the rate basis, policyholder equity, treatment of in-force contracts).
Where the guidelines are silent or the classification is genuinely arguable, log a pre-consultation question and route it to the Regulatory Affairs Manager for the FSA/Local Finance Bureau contact.
checklist.done: each provision type has a guideline reference and a note of the explanations the regulator will expect, or a logged pre-consultation question.

checklist.step: Confirm the calculation-method impact with the Appointed Actuary
actions: Take the tagged worksheet from Product Compliance and identify every row that changes the premium basis or the policy reserve method under Art. 116.

Run the affected product model and confirm whether the standard policy reserve regime (FSA Notification No. 48 of 1996 - standard mortality table and standard yield) still governs, or whether the change moves the product outside it.
State in writing whether contingency reserve category III for minimum-guarantee risk on the Variable Annuity is affected, and the direction of the impact.
Return a signed memorandum to Product Compliance confirming the calculation-method rows are complete and correctly described.
checklist.done: a signed Appointed Actuary memorandum confirms the calculation-method rows and states the standard-reserve and contingency-reserve III impact.

checklist.step: Determine the competent authority and lodgement channel per element
actions: For each AUTHORIZATION or NOTIFICATION row decide whether the application goes to the FSA Insurance Business Division or to the Director-General of the competent Local Finance Bureau, using the delegation table in the Ordinance for Enforcement.
Confirm the lodgement channel: the FSA Electronic Application and Notification System account, or paper submission with the prescribed number of counterparts.
Record the account holder, the authorised submitter and the counterpart count on each row.
Where the entity also writes the product in the United States, hand the row to the Regulatory Filing Specialist for the parallel state determination.
checklist.done: every filing row names its competent authority, lodgement channel and authorised submitter.

checklist.step: Run the parallel US state determination for the same change
actions: Log in to SERFF with the company instance, open Industry then Filing Rules, and select each state in which the product is written.
Choose the Business Type and the TOI/Sub-TOI from the NAIC Uniform Product Coding Matrix that matches the product (individual annuity - variable for the Variable Annuity line).
Read the state General Instructions and record the review method per state: prior approval, file-and-use, use-and-file, informational or exempt.
Check whether the form is covered by an IIPRC Uniform Standard and can go to the Compact instead of state by state, and record that decision.
Print each state instructions page to PDF named <state>-filing-rules-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf into the determination folder.
checklist.done: each US state has a recorded review method with a dated instructions capture, and the Compact-vs-state routing decision is written down.

checklist.step: Search the authorization history for coverage that already exists
actions: In the Internal Regulatory System open the Basic Document Register and search by product code and clause number for prior authorizations and notifications.
Open the closest prior authorization letter and compare the authorized wording and rate basis line by line with the proposed wording.
Decide reuse (no new filing) only where the authorized text and calculation basis are genuinely unchanged, and paste the prior authorization number and date onto the row.
In SERFF Filing Access run the same check for the US states by company, state, TOI and form number, and record the SERFF tracking number when reuse applies.
checklist.done: each row states either reuse with a prior authorization/SERFF tracking number or a new filing, based on an inspected prior approval.

checklist.step: Compute the earliest permissible sales-start date per element
actions: For AUTHORIZATION rows apply the FSA published standard processing period of 90 days for a basic-document amendment authorization and record it on the row.
Add internal lead times: application drafting days, actuarial review days, and a 20-business-day buffer for FSA supplementary questions.
Compute latest application date = intended sales-start date minus (90 days + question buffer + system implementation lead) and write it on the row.
For US prior-approval states apply that state's review/deemer days from the captured instructions and compute the same figure.
Load every latest application date into the Internal Regulatory System calendar with T-150 / T-120 / T-90 reminders.
checklist.done: every filing row shows the processing period, a computed latest application date and a calendar entry with reminders.

checklist.step: Name the exemption behind every 'no filing required' call
actions: For each OUT OF SCOPE row state the basis: the material is not a basic document under Art. 4(2), the change is a typographical correction with no substantive effect, or the provision is covered by an unchanged existing authorization.
Paste the statutory or ordinance citation supporting the basis together with its effective date.
Where the basis depends on a threshold or a scope test (for example sales-area or insured-scope limits in the statement of business procedures), record the tested value and its source.
Never leave a row reading only 'not required' - an unsupported row is treated as an AUTHORIZATION row until counsel says otherwise.
checklist.done: every out-of-scope row carries a named basis, a citation and, where relevant, the tested value.

checklist.step: Check whether the change triggers linked statutory obligations
actions: Test the change against the solicitation policy and solicitation-management obligations (Art. 294-2 and Art. 294-3) and record whether the sales process documentation must be updated.
Test whether the change alters figures that will appear in the Art. 110 business report or the Art. 111 explanatory disclosure documents, and notify the Statutory Reporting Manager if it does.
For Variable Annuity changes confirm whether the separate-account disclosure and the suitability standards for the channel need re-approval, and raise the task to Market Conduct.
Record each triggered obligation on the determination record with an owner and a due date.
checklist.done: linked solicitation, disclosure and reporting obligations are tested, and each triggered one has a named owner and due date.

checklist.step: Write the determination rows into the Filing Determination Log
actions: Add one log row per element per jurisdiction with: change id, entity, jurisdiction, basic document, clause reference, filing required Y/N, Art. 123(1)/123(2) classification, citation, competent authority, processing period, latest application date, reuse reference, decider and decision date.
Link every row to the determination folder holding the dated Art. 71 and SERFF captures and the Appointed Actuary memorandum.
Set row status to 'Determined - pending counsel' for notification-only and out-of-scope rows, otherwise 'Determined - closed'.
Run the log completeness report and clear any row with a blank citation or a blank latest application date before handover.
checklist.done: the log holds one complete, source-linked row per element per jurisdiction with no blank fields.

checklist.step: Obtain counsel sign-off on the classification calls
actions: Review every NOTIFICATION and OUT OF SCOPE row against the Art. 71 enumerated item or exemption basis quoted on it.
Re-read the cited ordinance text yourself rather than relying on the pasted quote, and confirm or overturn the classification in writing on the row.
Send overturned rows back to Product Compliance the same week with the corrected classification and the reason.
Stamp confirmed rows with counsel name and date and move them to 'Determined - closed'.
checklist.done: no notification-only or out-of-scope row is closed without a dated counsel confirmation of the citation.

checklist.step: Publish the determination and arm the pre-use release gate
actions: Attach the determination summary to the product change record and to the release plan.

Set a hard release gate on every AUTHORIZATION row: no policy may be sold on the changed provision in that jurisdiction until the FSA authorization letter or state approval is recorded against the row.
Give the implementation team the per-jurisdiction earliest-use dates so policy admin and rating effective dates are configured to them.
Book the filing milestones into the product launch plan and confirm the launch date is still achievable in writing.
checklist.done: the product change record shows a per-jurisdiction earliest-use date and every authorization row is blocked in the release plan.

checklist.step: File the determination evidence for the retention period
actions: Move the determination folder (worksheet, Art. 71 and SERFF captures, Appointed Actuary memorandum, counsel sign-offs, log export) into the compliance evidence repository under REG-030 and the product code.
Apply the 10-years-from-provision-withdrawal retention label so the record survives product sunset and any later FSA inspection.
Confirm the repository index makes the record searchable by product code, clause number, authorization number and SERFF tracking number.
Record the archive location back on the determination log row.
checklist.done: the determination record is archived, labelled for 10-year retention and retrievable by product code and authorization number.

testing.step: Build the population of basic-document provisions that changed in the quarter
actions: Extract from the Internal Regulatory System version history every statement of business procedures, policy condition and calculation-method provision with a version effective date inside the quarter, by entity.
Add every product and rider whose sales-start date fell in the quarter from the product launch calendar, so a launch on an unversioned provision cannot hide.
Reconcile the extract to the product committee minutes for the quarter and resolve every difference before sampling.
Sign the population as complete and record the extraction query and date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the population reconciles to the product committee minutes and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile every changed provision to a determination that pre-dates its use
actions: Match each population row to a Filing Determination Log row on change id plus jurisdiction plus clause reference.
Confirm the determination decision date is earlier than the provision's sales-start date.
List unmatched rows and determinations dated after first sale as automatic exceptions with no judgement applied.
Quantify the exposure on each unmatched row: number of policies sold on the provision and total first-year premium.
testing.done: every population row is matched to a pre-dated determination or listed as an exception with its policy-count exposure.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of rows classified AUTHORIZATION and 100% of Variable Annuity minimum-guarantee and separate-account rows.
Take 25 rows at random using a seeded, reproducible selection from the remaining population, with a minimum total sample of 40 rows.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be redrawn.
Confirm the sample covers every entity and both the FSA and Local Finance Bureau routing paths.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers all authorization and Variable Annuity guarantee rows.

testing.step: Re-perform the Art. 123 classification independently
actions: Read the Ordinance for Enforcement Art. 71 text as it stood on the determination date, from e-Gov's dated version, before opening the worksheet.
Reach your own AUTHORIZATION / NOTIFICATION / OUT OF SCOPE conclusion for each sampled row and write it down first.
Compare with the recorded classification; treat 'right answer, wrong enumerated item' as an exception because the wrong item means the wrong text was read.
Capture the dated ordinance text you relied on into the workpaper alongside your conclusion.
testing.done: each sampled row carries an independent classification conclusion and the dated source text behind it.

testing.step: Test the actuarial completeness of the calculation-method rows
actions: For each sampled product open the model version in force before and after the change and diff the premium basis, mortality table, valuation interest rate and reserve method.
Confirm every difference found in the model appears as a calculation-method row on the determination worksheet.
Confirm the Appointed Actuary memorandum on file addresses the standard policy reserve regime and contingency reserve category III where the model shows an impact.
Report any model difference with no matching worksheet row as an exception - that is an unfiled calculation-method change.
testing.done: every modelled change to the premium or reserve basis maps to a worksheet row, or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Test the support behind every 'no filing required' call
actions: Pull each sampled OUT OF SCOPE row and read the cited statutory or ordinance provision as it read on the determination date.
Confirm the basis actually covers the element it was applied to, including any scope test on insured population or sales area and the value that was tested.
Confirm a dated counsel sign-off exists and pre-dates the sales-start date.
Treat a generic 'not a basic document' with no citation as a fail rather than a documentation gap.
testing.done: every out-of-scope row is supported by a verified citation, a tested scope value and a pre-dated counsel sign-off.

testing.step: Trace filing-required rows to a lodged application or notification
actions: For each sampled AUTHORIZATION row obtain the application receipt from the FSA Electronic Application and Notification System and the authorization letter, and check the authorized wording matches the provision in use.
For each NOTIFICATION row obtain the dated notification receipt and confirm it pre-dates first sale.
For US rows search the recorded SERFF tracking number in SERFF Filing Access and confirm company, state, TOI, form number and disposition.
Capture the receipt or SERFF filing detail screen into the workpaper for every traced row.
testing.done: every filing-required row traces to a lodged application or notification that pre-dates first sale, with the receipt captured.

testing.step: Recompute the processing-period maths and prove the gate held
actions: For 10 sampled authorization rows recompute latest application date = sales-start date minus (90-day standard processing period + question buffer + implementation lead).
Compare the actual application date to the recomputed date and note every application lodged later than it.
Check the policy admin and illustration effective date for the provision is on or after the authorization letter date.
Treat any sale on an authorization-class provision before the authorization date as a reportable breach and not a test exception, and notify the Head of Compliance the same day.
testing.done: no sampled provision was sold before authorization and the processing-period maths reconciles for every recomputed row.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with change id, entity, clause reference, what was missed and the policyholder impact.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list (intake missed the change, wrong Art. 71 item, stale ordinance text, calculation-method change not surfaced by Actuarial, launch date crushed) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any sale-before-authorization, open a self-report assessment with General Counsel covering the Art. 128 reporting and Art. 315 penalty exposure.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a tracker issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-unfiled-provision threshold and split it by entity and by classification type.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored none of the sampled determinations and does not sit in Product Compliance, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any self-report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-030.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Product Compliance assembles and owns the completeness of the basic-document amendment package; the Appointed Actuary owns the reserve sections covering Art. 116 policy reserves and Art. 117 outstanding claims reserves including IBNR

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Insurance Business Act Art. 117 (outstanding claims reserve including incurred-but-not-reported), Art. 116 with Ordinance for Enforcement Art. 69 (premium reserve, unearned premium, refund reserve, contingency reserve categories I-III), and Arts. 97, 98 and 100 (permitted business and asset-management restrictions), each re-read on e-Gov at package assembly and reconciled to FSA Notification No. 48 of 1996 on standard policy reserves

In-scope processes.value: Filing package assembly for every basic-document amendment: application form, reasons statement, before/after comparison table of the affected clauses, actuarial memorandum with the Art. 116 reserve method and the Art. 117 outstanding-claims and IBNR basis, and the per-state SERFF checklists for the parallel US filings

In-scope systems.value: Reserve exhibits and sensitivity runs produced in the actuarial modelling platform and reconciled to the general ledger; package assembled and version-controlled in the Internal Regulatory System

Compliance procedure documented.value: Basic-Document Amendment Package Procedure JP-116/117: mandatory contents list, actuarial memorandum template with the Art. 69 reserve category schedule, IBNR method statement under Enforcement Regulation Art. 73, asset-management compliance attestation under Arts. 97-100, and the SERFF companion-item checklist for US states

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary and the Head of Compliance; refreshed each year before the March 31 business-year-end valuation cycle and on any FSA notification revising the standard valuation basis

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Package must be complete and internally signed at least 10 business days before the latest application date computed at determination, so the 90-day FSA standard processing period is not eaten by assembly; reserve exhibits are refreshed to the most recent business-year-end (March 31) or quarter-end valuation

Deadline reminders configured.value: Internal Regulatory System package tasks with individual owner due dates for each companion item, alerting the owner at T-20 and the Product Filing Specialist at T-10 business days before the latest application date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: The as-submitted package, every superseded draft, the model run identifiers behind the reserve exhibits and the reconciliation to the general ledger retained 10 years from the business year of submission

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any package lodged with a missing mandatory item, an unreconciled reserve exhibit or an unsigned actuarial memorandum is logged as an exception with root cause and a corrective resubmission date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Chief Actuary signs off any re-issued reserve exhibit or corrected actuarial memorandum before it is resubmitted to the FSA

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every basic-document amendment package lodged with the FSA or a Local Finance Bureau during the business year, plus every SERFF submission for the same product change, taken from the filing log

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Fail if any mandatory package item is absent, if a reserve exhibit does not tie to the general ledger within the 0.1% tolerance, if the IBNR method described differs from the method actually run, or if the actuarial memorandum is unsigned; more than one fail in the year is reported as a control deficiency

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per filing with an annual reserve refresh cycle; the test runs annually after the March 31 business-year-end close over all packages lodged in that business year, with 100% coverage of packages containing a reserve-method change

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must be outside Actuarial and Product Compliance and must not have prepared or peer-reviewed any sampled package

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual package-completeness workpaper with the package inventory, the checklist re-performance grid and the ledger reconciliations, filed in the compliance evidence repository under REG-030 by business year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The as-lodged package plus the model run identifiers, the ledger reconciliation and the Appointed Actuary opinion, producible for an FSA on-site inspection or an Art. 128 report request within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Affairs Manager routes FSA supplementary questions on the package to the Appointed Actuary for reserve content and to Product Compliance for wording content; the Chief Actuary clears every reserve answer before it is sent

checklist.step: Open the package shell from the determination and load the mandatory contents list
actions: In the Internal Regulatory System open the closed determination row and create the package shell against it, inheriting entity, competent authority and latest application date.

Load the JP-116/117 mandatory contents list: application form, statement of reasons, before/after clause comparison table, marked-up basic documents, actuarial memorandum, reserve exhibits, asset-management attestation, and the corporate authority evidence.
Assign each item an owner (Product Compliance, Appointed Actuary, Investment, Corporate Secretary) and a due date 10 business days before the latest application date.
Notify each owner through the Internal Regulatory System task and confirm acceptance in writing.
checklist.done: the package shell exists with every mandatory item listed, owned and dated ahead of the latest application date.

checklist.step: Produce the before/after clause comparison for the amended basic documents
actions: Pull the currently authorized wording for each affected clause from the Basic Document Register and place it in the left column of the comparison table.
Place the proposed wording in the right column and mark every insertion, deletion and renumbering.
Write a one-line reason for each change in the third column, referencing the product committee decision that drove it.
Confirm clause numbering, cross-references and defined terms remain consistent across the whole document after the change, and fix any broken cross-reference before the table is issued.
Send the table to Regulatory Counsel for a wording read before it goes into the package.
checklist.done: a complete before/after table exists for every amended clause with a reason and no broken cross-references.

checklist.step: Refresh the policy reserve exhibits under Art. 116 and Ordinance Art. 69
actions: Run the affected product model at the most recent business-year-end (March 31) or quarter-end valuation date and produce the reserve exhibit split by the Ordinance for Enforcement Art. 69 categories: premium reserve, unearned premium, refund reserve and contingency reserve categories I, II and III.

State the valuation basis on the exhibit: mortality table (standard mortality table where the standard policy reserve regime applies), standard valuation interest rate, and the FSA Notification No. 48 of 1996 reference.
Show the reserve on the current basis and on the proposed basis side by side, with the movement attributed to the change.
Record the model version, run identifier, data cut date and parameter set on the exhibit footer so the run is reproducible.
Have the model result peer-reviewed by a second actuary and record the reviewer name and date.
checklist.done: a peer-reviewed reserve exhibit exists by Art. 69 category showing current and proposed basis with a reproducible run identifier.

checklist.step: Produce the outstanding claims and IBNR exhibit under Art. 117
actions: Extract the claims data cut at the valuation date from the claims platform and reconcile the paid and case-reserve totals to the general ledger before running anything.

Run the outstanding claims reserve split into case reserves for claims reported and payable, and the incurred-but-not-reported element computed on the statistical basis prescribed under the Ordinance for Enforcement Art. 73 and the associated FSA notification.
Show the IBNR calculation inputs on the exhibit: the periods used, the average payment ratio, and any judgemental loading with its rationale.
State on the exhibit whether the product change alters claim reporting patterns or benefit triggers, and quantify the effect on the IBNR if it does.
Reconcile the total Art. 117 reserve on the exhibit to the ledger balance and document any difference above 0.1%.
checklist.done: the Art. 117 exhibit shows case and IBNR components with the prescribed statistical basis and ties to the ledger within tolerance.

checklist.step: Write the actuarial memorandum
actions: Describe the premium basis of the amended product: mortality, morbidity, lapse, expense and interest assumptions, and the source and vintage of each.
Describe the policy reserve method by Art. 69 category and state expressly whether the standard policy reserve regime applies, and if not, why and what basis is used instead.
Describe the Art. 117 outstanding claims and IBNR method and cross-reference the exhibit run identifier.
For the Variable Annuity, describe the contingency reserve category III basis for minimum-guarantee risk and the scenario set used to size it.
Certify that the reserves are adequate and the premium basis is not unfairly discriminatory, sign and date the memorandum, and pass it to the Chief Actuary for counter-signature.
checklist.done: a signed and counter-signed actuarial memorandum covers the premium basis, the Art. 69 reserve categories, the Art. 117 IBNR basis and the guarantee reserve.

checklist.step: Attest the asset-management position under Arts. 97, 98 and 100
actions: Pull the current portfolio position by asset class and counterparty from the investment platform at the valuation date.

Confirm the assets backing the amended product fall within the permitted asset-management scope of Art. 97 and the ancillary business scope of Art. 98, and identify anything requiring separate treatment.
Confirm no prohibited activity under Art. 100 is implicated by the product change, in particular any arrangement that would tie insurance acceptance to another transaction.
For the Variable Annuity separate account, list the fund menu and confirm each fund is eligible for separate-account investment and matches the fund list in the policy conditions.
Sign a one-page attestation with the position date and attach the supporting position report.
checklist.done: a signed, dated asset-management attestation covering Arts. 97, 98 and 100 with the separate-account fund menu is in the package.

checklist.step: Reconcile every exhibit in the package to the general ledger
actions: Take the Art. 116 policy reserve total and the Art. 117 outstanding claims total from the exhibits and pull the corresponding ledger balances at the same valuation date.
Build a reconciliation showing exhibit total, ledger total, difference and explanation for each reserve line.
Clear any difference above the 0.1% tolerance with Actuarial before the package can move forward - do not annotate it and proceed.
Sign the reconciliation and attach it behind the exhibits in the package.
checklist.done: every reserve exhibit ties to the ledger within 0.1% and the signed reconciliation sits behind it in the package.

checklist.step: Draft the application form and statement of reasons
actions: Complete the FSA basic-document amendment application form: applicant name and registration number, the basic documents affected, the clauses amended, the intended effective date and the Art. 123 provision relied on.

Write the statement of reasons covering the business need, the effect on existing policyholders, the transitional treatment of in-force contracts, and why the amendment does not harm policyholder protection.
Address in the statement each review viewpoint flagged from the FSA Comprehensive Supervisory Guidelines Part II-4 at determination.
Have Regulatory Counsel read the statement of reasons and sign the draft before it is finalised.
checklist.done: the application form is complete and the statement of reasons addresses in-force treatment and every flagged guideline viewpoint, with counsel sign-off.

checklist.step: Assemble the parallel US state package and per-state checklists
actions: For each state on the determination, open the SERFF filing-requirements checklist for the TOI and list the companion items: cover letter, Statement of Variability, actuarial memorandum and certification, readability certification, rate/rule schedule, third-party filer authorization and the filing fee amount and payment method.
Map each companion item to the Japan package equivalent where one exists and identify the items that must be produced separately for the state.
Confirm every PDF is text-searchable, unwatermarked, carries the form number and edition date on each page and sits under the SERFF per-attachment size limit.
Start the long-lead items now - readability scoring, translated forms and third-party filer authorization - and record their owners and due dates.
checklist.done: each state has a completed companion-item checklist with owners, due dates and SERFF-compliant attachments.

checklist.step: Attach the corporate authority and licence evidence
actions: Pull from the board portal the board or executive committee resolution approving the product and the basic-document amendment, and extract the certified minute.
Attach the current insurance business licence certificate under Art. 3(1) and the entity registration particulars showing the licence class and permitted lines.
Confirm the person signing the application holds the delegated authority recorded in the delegation of authority schedule, and attach that schedule page.
Certify each attachment as a true copy with date and seal.
checklist.done: certified board authority, the Art. 3(1) licence certificate and evidence of the signatory's delegated authority are in the package.

checklist.step: Run the package completeness review against the mandatory contents list
actions: Walk the JP-116/117 mandatory contents list item by item and mark each present, absent or draft.
Reject the package back to the item owner if anything is marked draft, unsigned, or dated before the current valuation cut.

Check every internal cross-reference resolves: the memorandum cites the exhibit run identifiers, the exhibits cite the model version, the comparison table cites the clause numbers used in the application form.
Record the completeness review outcome, reviewer and date on the package shell.
checklist.done: the completeness review is recorded with every mandatory item present, signed and internally cross-referenced.

checklist.step: Peer-review the actuarial content independently of the preparer
actions: Confirm the model version used for the exhibits is the approved production version recorded in the model governance repository, and not a development build.
Check the model's last validation date and any open validation findings that touch the reserve method being filed.
Re-run one exhibit line from the stated inputs and confirm it reproduces the filed figure.
Write a short review note stating scope, findings and whether the actuarial content is fit to file, and attach it to the package.
checklist.done: an independent review note confirms the model version, validation status and reproducibility of at least one filed figure.

checklist.step: Freeze and version the package for lodgement
actions: Lock the package version in the Internal Regulatory System and generate the as-submitted manifest listing every file with its name, page count and checksum.
Convert the package to the file formats and naming convention the FSA Electronic Application and Notification System accepts, and verify each file opens from the manifest.
Record the frozen version id on the determination log row so the determination, package and later disposition all share one thread.
Circulate the frozen package to the Appointed Actuary, Regulatory Counsel and Regulatory Affairs Manager for final release to lodge.
checklist.done: a locked, manifest-backed package version exists in the accepted formats with the version id written onto the determination row.

checklist.step: Prepare the anticipated-questions file before lodgement
actions: List the questions the FSA has raised on comparable amendments in the last three years from the regulator correspondence archive.
Draft a holding answer and name the answer owner for each, covering reserve adequacy, in-force policyholder treatment, guarantee charge justification and distribution suitability.
Pre-agree with the Appointed Actuary which sensitivity runs would be produced on request, and have them staged in the model so they can be delivered inside a week.
File the anticipated-questions sheet with the package so whoever handles the response is not starting cold.
checklist.done: an anticipated-questions sheet with named answer owners and pre-staged sensitivity runs sits with the frozen package.

checklist.step: Archive the as-submitted package and its supporting evidence
actions: Move the frozen package, the manifest, the superseded drafts and the ledger reconciliation into the compliance evidence repository under REG-030, entity and business year.
Apply the 10-years-from-business-year retention label and mark the record as inspection-relevant so it is surfaced in FSA on-site inspection preparation.
Index the record by product code, clause reference, model run identifier and application number.
Write the archive reference back onto the package shell and the determination log row.
checklist.done: the as-submitted package is archived under a 10-year label and indexed by product code, clause and model run identifier.

testing.step: Build the population of packages lodged in the business year
actions: Extract from the Internal Regulatory System every basic-document amendment package with a lodgement date between April 1 and March 31 of the business year, by entity and competent authority.
Add every SERFF submission for the same product changes taken from the SERFF filing list export.
Reconcile the count to the regulator correspondence log of application receipts and resolve every difference before sampling.
Sign the population as complete and record the extraction parameters in the workpaper.
testing.done: the package population reconciles to the receipt correspondence log and is signed complete.

testing.step: Reconcile each lodged package to a frozen version and manifest
actions: Match each population row to a frozen package version id and its as-submitted manifest.
Verify the manifest checksums against the archived files so the archived package is provably the lodged one.
List packages with no frozen version, no manifest, or a checksum mismatch as automatic exceptions.
Confirm each package version id also appears on its determination log row so the thread is unbroken.
testing.done: every lodged package matches an archived, checksum-verified frozen version linked to its determination row.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of packages containing a policy reserve method change, an IBNR method change or a Variable Annuity guarantee change.
Take 15 further packages by seeded random selection from the remainder, with a minimum total of 25 packages or the whole population if smaller.
Record the seed, population size, stratification rule and selection date so the sample can be redrawn.
Confirm the sample includes at least one package routed to a Local Finance Bureau and one parallel SERFF submission.
testing.done: a reproducible sample is drawn covering all reserve-method changes and both regulator routing paths.

testing.step: Re-perform the mandatory contents check on the sample
actions: Open the archived package and tick the JP-116/117 mandatory contents list yourself without reading the preparer's completeness review.
Confirm every signature block is executed and dated, and that no document is watermarked draft.
Confirm the actuarial memorandum is signed by the Appointed Actuary and counter-signed by the Chief Actuary before the lodgement date.
Record any absent or unsigned mandatory item as a fail regardless of whether the application was later authorized.
testing.done: each sampled package has an independent contents grid with every mandatory item confirmed present, signed and dated pre-lodgement.

testing.step: Re-perform the reserve exhibit reconciliation to the ledger
actions: Pull the general ledger balances for policy reserves and outstanding claims reserves at each sampled package's stated valuation date.
Compare them to the Art. 116 and Art. 117 totals on the filed exhibits and compute the difference as a percentage.
Confirm any difference above 0.1% carries a cleared explanation signed by the Statutory Reporting Manager before lodgement, not after.
Capture the ledger query output and the comparison into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled exhibit is independently tied to the ledger within 0.1% or the pre-lodgement clearance is evidenced.

testing.step: Re-perform the IBNR calculation described in the memorandum
actions: Read the IBNR method as described in the sampled actuarial memorandum, including the periods, the average payment ratio and any loading.
Re-run the calculation from the archived data cut using only what the memorandum describes.
Compare your result to the filed figure and treat any material difference as a fail - the memorandum must describe the method that was actually used.
Confirm the statistical basis used matches the Ordinance for Enforcement Art. 73 requirement and the associated FSA notification in force at the valuation date.
testing.done: the described IBNR method reproduces the filed figure and matches the prescribed statistical basis, or the difference is logged as a fail.

testing.step: Trace the asset-management attestation to the underlying positions
actions: Pull the portfolio position report at the attestation date from the investment platform.
Confirm the asset classes named in the Arts. 97/98/100 attestation match the actual holdings backing the product.
For Variable Annuity packages compare the separate-account fund menu in the attestation to the fund list printed in the filed policy conditions, fund by fund.
Log any fund present in one list and absent from the other as an exception, and quantify the assets involved.
testing.done: the attestation is traced to actual holdings and the separate-account fund menu agrees with the filed policy conditions.

testing.step: Test the model provenance behind the filed exhibits
actions: Take the model version and run identifier from each sampled exhibit footer and look them up in the model governance repository.
Confirm the version was the approved production version on the run date and was not superseded or under remediation.
Check for open validation findings dated before lodgement that touch the filed reserve method, and confirm they were disclosed to the Appointed Actuary.
Record any exhibit produced on an unapproved or expired model version as an exception with the reserve amount affected.
testing.done: every sampled exhibit is proven to come from an approved production model version with validation findings disclosed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the package, the missing or defective item and the regulatory consequence.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list (item owner missed the due date, exhibit not refreshed to the valuation date, memorandum describes a superseded method, ledger difference not cleared, unapproved model version) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where a lodged package was materially defective, agree with the Regulatory Affairs Manager whether a corrective submission to the FSA is required and by when.
Carry every open exception into the next annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a tracker issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a decision on corrective resubmission.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the package defect rate against the zero-missing-mandatory-item threshold and split it by defect type.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) citing the workpaper reference for each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared and peer-reviewed none of the sampled packages and sits outside Actuarial and Product Compliance, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any corrective resubmissions to the Audit Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-030.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, defect rate and Audit Committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: The filing analyst in Regulatory Filing lodges every submission and owns it until disposition; the Chief Investment Officer owns the Art. 115 price fluctuation reserve figures carried inside it

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Insurance Business Act Art. 115 (price fluctuation reserve on stocks and other price-variable assets, accumulation rates and restricted drawdown), Art. 116 and Art. 117, checked against the current Ordinance for Enforcement accumulation-rate table and the FSA notification setting the reserve limit, dated at submission

In-scope processes.value: Lodgement and disposition tracking for every FSA basic-document application and notification and every parallel SERFF state submission, including the annual price fluctuation reserve accrual and any application to draw the reserve down under Art. 115(2)

In-scope systems.value: SERFF for the US state submissions and the FSA Electronic Application and Notification System for Japan; both dispositions written back to the filing log in the Internal Regulatory System

Compliance procedure documented.value: Submission and Disposition Tracking Procedure: pre-lodgement checks, channel-specific lodgement steps, receipt capture, weekly open-filing review, objection triage, disposition capture and write-back to the determination row and the release gate

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Regulatory Affairs Manager; re-approved annually and whenever the FSA Electronic Application and Notification System or SERFF changes its submission requirements

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Lodgement on or before the latest application date computed at determination; the FSA 90-day standard processing period is tracked from the receipt date; the Art. 115 reserve accrual is computed at the March 31 business year end and carried into the statutory accounts filed with the Art. 110 business report within 3 months of year end

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing log alerts at lodgement due date, at day 30 and day 60 of the FSA processing period with no substantive contact, and at 3 business days before any objection response due date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Submission receipt with date and time, the as-lodged file set, every regulator communication and the final disposition letter retained 10 years from the business year of disposition

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Late lodgement, a submission rejected for form, a lapsed objection deadline or a disposition not written back to the release gate is logged as an exception with root cause and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Regulatory Affairs Manager signs off every re-lodgement after a rejection and every filing lodged after its latest application date

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every FSA application and notification and every SERFF submission lodged in the period, taken from the filing log and independently from the SERFF filing list export and the FSA electronic system submission history

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Fail if a submission has no captured receipt, if the lodged file set differs from the frozen package manifest, if a disposition is not recorded within 5 business days of the regulator issuing it, or if the Art. 115 reserve figure in the submission differs from the ledger; zero tolerance on undispatched filings past their latest application date

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per filing with an annual price fluctuation reserve accrual; the test runs quarterly on lodgement and disposition hygiene and annually after the March 31 year end on the Art. 115 reserve figures

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have lodged or tracked any sampled submission and must sit outside Regulatory Filing

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly lodgement-and-disposition workpaper and the annual price fluctuation reserve tie-out, both filed in the compliance evidence repository under REG-030

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Filing log export with receipt numbers, FSA application numbers, SERFF tracking numbers, submission dates and dispositions, plus the Art. 115 reserve computation, producible for an FSA inspection or a market conduct exam within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Affairs Manager holds the FSA and Local Finance Bureau relationship; the Regulatory Filing Specialist answers SERFF objections; the Chief Investment Officer clears any answer touching the price fluctuation reserve rates or drawdown

checklist.step: Run the pre-lodgement gate on the frozen package
actions: Open the frozen package version and compare the file list to the as-submitted manifest, checking name, page count and checksum for every file.
Confirm the determination row shows the competent authority, the classification and a latest application date that has not passed.
Confirm the Appointed Actuary, Regulatory Counsel and Regulatory Affairs Manager have all released the package to lodge.
Record the pre-lodgement gate result on the filing log row, and stop the lodgement if any check fails rather than filing and fixing later.
checklist.done: the pre-lodgement gate is recorded as passed with the manifest verified and all three releases in place.

checklist.step: Confirm the price fluctuation reserve figures carried in the submission
actions: Pull the book value of price-variable assets at the valuation date by class from the investment platform: domestic equities, bonds, foreign-currency-denominated assets and real estate.

Apply the accumulation rate for each class from the current Ordinance for Enforcement table - read the table as it stands rather than reusing last year's rates - and compute the required annual accrual.
Compare the accumulated balance to the statutory accumulation ceiling for each class and flag any class that has reached it.

Where the reserve is being drawn down, evidence that the drawdown offsets realised losses exceeding the prescribed threshold under Art. 115(2) and note whether FSA approval is required for any other use.
Sign the computation and hand it to the Regulatory Filing Specialist to attach to the submission.
checklist.done: a signed Art. 115 computation by asset class, with rates read from the current table and drawdown basis evidenced, is attached to the submission.

checklist.step: Tie the reserve figures in the submission to the general ledger
actions: Pull the price fluctuation reserve, policy reserve and outstanding claims reserve ledger balances at the valuation date.
Compare each to the corresponding figure in the submission and record the difference.
Clear differences with Investment and Actuarial before lodgement and sign the tie-out sheet.
Attach the signed tie-out sheet behind the reserve exhibits in the submission.
checklist.done: the submission's reserve figures tie to the ledger and the signed tie-out sheet is attached.

checklist.step: Lodge the Japan application through the FSA electronic channel
actions: Sign in to the FSA Electronic Application and Notification System with the entity account and the authorised submitter credential recorded on the determination row.

Select the correct procedure - basic-document amendment authorization under Art. 123(1) or notification under Art. 123(2) - and the receiving office (FSA Insurance Business Division or the competent Local Finance Bureau).
Complete the applicant particulars, attach the package files in the manifest order and confirm each upload succeeded before submitting.
Submit and immediately download the submission receipt showing the application number, receiving office, date and time.
Where paper counterparts are also required, dispatch them by recorded delivery the same day and file the dispatch proof.
checklist.done: the application is lodged, the receipt with application number and timestamp is downloaded, and any paper counterparts are dispatched with proof.

checklist.step: Lodge the parallel US state submissions in SERFF
actions: In SERFF create the filing from the company instance, set Business Type, TOI and Sub-TOI from the coding matrix and add the target states.
Complete the General Information tab (filing description, effective date requested, previous filing reference) and the Rate/Rule and Form schedules.
Attach the supporting documents against the state's required document types and pay the filing fee by the method the state accepts (EFT where offered).
Submit to each state and record the SERFF Tracking Number and submission date for each on the filing log row.
Where a state takes the line outside SERFF, lodge on the state portal or by paper per the captured instructions and record the confirmation number.
checklist.done: each state has a submitted filing with its SERFF tracking number or portal confirmation recorded on the filing log.

checklist.step: Write the lodgement particulars back to the filing log and the release gate
actions: Record on the filing log row: application number or SERFF tracking number, receiving office, lodgement date and time, submitter, and the frozen package version id.
Start the processing clock on the row using the FSA 90-day standard processing period or the state review/deemer days.
Confirm the release gate on the product change record still reads BLOCKED for every authorization-class jurisdiction.
Attach the receipt PDF to the row so the receipt and the package share one record.
checklist.done: every lodged submission has a log row with identifiers, a running processing clock, an attached receipt and a blocked release gate.

checklist.step: Hold the weekly open-filing review
actions: Run the open-filing report from the filing log showing every submission without a disposition, with days elapsed against the processing clock.
Chase any FSA application at day 60 of the 90-day standard processing period with no substantive contact, through the named case officer.
Chase any SERFF filing sitting past the state's stated review period, using the SERFF Note to Reviewer function so the chase is on the filing record.
Record the chase, the response and the revised expectation on the log row - never chase by phone without writing it back.
checklist.done: every open filing has a dated status entry from the current week and every overdue one has an evidenced chase.

checklist.step: Triage incoming regulator communications the day they arrive
actions: Check the FSA electronic system inbox and the SERFF Correspondence tab every business day and download anything new.
Classify each item as an acknowledgement, a supplementary question, a formal objection, a request to withdraw and refile, or a disposition.
Log the item on the filing row with its receipt date and compute the response due date from the regulator's stated deadline.
Route supplementary questions to the answer owner named on the anticipated-questions sheet and notify them the same day.
checklist.done: every regulator communication is downloaded, classified, logged with a computed response due date and routed the day it arrives.

checklist.step: Escalate a stalled or at-risk filing before it costs the launch date
actions: Compare the projected disposition date on each open filing to the intended sales-start date weekly.
Where the launch date is no longer reachable, escalate in writing to the Insurance Product Manager and the Head of Compliance within one business day.
Put the options in writing: move the sales-start date, launch without the jurisdiction, or launch on the currently authorized wording - never launch ahead of authorization.
Record the decision, its owner and its date on the filing log row and update the release plan.
checklist.done: every at-risk filing has a written, owned decision that keeps the jurisdiction either compliant or out of the launch.

checklist.step: Capture the disposition and its exact terms
actions: Download the FSA authorization letter or the notification acceptance, or the SERFF disposition report, on the day it is issued.
Record the disposition type, the disposition date, the authorized effective date, and any condition or undertaking the regulator attached.
Compare the authorized wording and rate basis to the as-lodged version and flag any regulator-driven amendment for re-issue of the basic document.
Where a filing was disapproved or withdrawn, record the stated reason verbatim - it drives the next attempt.
checklist.done: the disposition, its date, its authorized effective date and any attached conditions are recorded and compared to the as-lodged version.

checklist.step: Release the gate only against a recorded disposition
actions: Take the recorded disposition and set the jurisdiction's earliest-use date to the authorized effective date, never earlier.
Change the release gate from BLOCKED to RELEASED on that jurisdiction only, leaving every other jurisdiction blocked.
Pass any regulator condition or undertaking to the owning function with a due date before first sale.
Notify Distribution and Policy Administration of the confirmed earliest-use date in writing.
checklist.done: the gate is released per jurisdiction against a recorded disposition, with conditions assigned and the earliest-use date communicated.

checklist.step: Book the price fluctuation reserve movement into the accounts
actions: Post the Art. 115 accrual computed by Investment into the March 31 business-year-end close, by asset class, with the computation attached to the journal.
Confirm the posted balance does not exceed the statutory accumulation ceiling for any class.
Carry the balance and the movement into the statutory accounts that accompany the Art. 110 business report submitted within 3 months of the business year end.
Reconcile the disclosed figure to the ledger and to the figure carried in any related regulatory submission.
checklist.done: the Art. 115 reserve movement is posted, within ceiling, and reconciles across the ledger, the statutory accounts and the submission.

checklist.step: Reconcile the filing log to the regulator systems monthly
actions: Export the SERFF filing list for the company instance and the FSA electronic system submission history for the month.
Match both exports to the filing log on tracking number and application number and list anything present in one and not the other.
Investigate every unmatched item - a filing lodged outside the log is as serious as a logged filing never lodged.
Sign the reconciliation and file it with the month's evidence.
checklist.done: the filing log reconciles to both regulator system exports with every difference investigated and the reconciliation signed.

checklist.step: Close the filing record and hand the thread to the archive
actions: Set the filing row to CLOSED only when the disposition, the authorized effective date, the conditions and the gate release are all recorded.
Confirm the row links back to the determination row and forward to the archived package and disposition letter.
Run the closure completeness check for the month and clear any row closed with a missing disposition document.
Hand the closed set to Records for archival.
checklist.done: every closed filing row carries a disposition document, an authorized effective date and unbroken links to determination and archive.

checklist.step: Archive receipts, correspondence and dispositions
actions: Move the submission receipts, all regulator correspondence, the disposition letters and the Art. 115 computation into the compliance evidence repository under REG-030, entity and business year.
Apply the 10-years-from-disposition retention label and mark the record inspection-relevant.
Index by application number, SERFF tracking number, product code and disposition date.
Write the archive reference back to the filing log row.
checklist.done: receipts, correspondence and dispositions are archived under a 10-year label and indexed by application and tracking number.

testing.step: Build the population of submissions from the regulator systems, not the log
actions: Export the SERFF filing list for every company instance for the period, including withdrawn and disapproved filings.
Export the FSA Electronic Application and Notification System submission history for the same period and entity.
Combine both into the population so that submissions missing from the internal filing log are still in scope.
Sign the population as complete and record both export dates and parameters in the workpaper.
testing.done: the population is built from regulator system exports and signed complete independently of the internal log.

testing.step: Reconcile the regulator population to the internal filing log
actions: Match each regulator record to a filing log row on application number or SERFF tracking number.
List submissions present in the regulator system with no log row, and log rows with no regulator record, as automatic exceptions.
For each unmatched item establish whether a filing was made outside the control process or a logged filing was never lodged.
Quantify the exposure: product, jurisdiction and whether sales occurred in the interim.
testing.done: every regulator record matches a log row or is listed as an exception with its exposure quantified.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of Art. 123(1) authorization submissions, all disapproved or withdrawn filings, and all filings lodged after their latest application date.
Take 20 further submissions by seeded random selection from the remainder, minimum total 35.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date so the sample can be redrawn.
Confirm coverage of both the FSA channel and SERFF, and of at least one Local Finance Bureau submission.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all authorization, late and adverse-disposition filings is drawn and documented.

testing.step: Verify the lodged file set against the frozen manifest
actions: For each sampled SERFF filing open the Filing Access record and list the attached documents with their upload dates.
For each sampled FSA application open the submission history entry and list the attached files.
Compare each list to the frozen package manifest file by file and record any file lodged that was not in the manifest or any manifest file not lodged.
Capture the regulator-side document list into the workpaper as the evidence.
testing.done: the lodged file set matches the frozen manifest for every sampled submission, or the difference is captured and logged.

testing.step: Recompute the price fluctuation reserve carried in the submissions
actions: Pull the book value of price-variable assets by class at the valuation date independently of the preparer's extract.
Apply the accumulation rates from the Ordinance for Enforcement table in force at that date and recompute the required accrual by class.
Compare your figure to the filed figure and to the posted ledger balance, and test the accumulated balance against the statutory ceiling for each class.
Where a drawdown occurred, verify the realised losses exceeded the prescribed threshold under Art. 115(2) and that any other use carried FSA approval.
Record any difference above 0.1% as an exception with the amount and the class.
testing.done: the Art. 115 accrual is independently recomputed and agrees with the filed and posted figures within 0.1%, with drawdowns justified.

testing.step: Recompute the lodgement timing against the latest application date
actions: For each sampled submission take the latest application date from the determination row and the actual lodgement timestamp from the receipt.
Recompute latest application date = intended sales-start date minus (90-day FSA standard processing period or state review days, plus question buffer, plus implementation lead).
Flag every submission lodged after its recomputed latest application date and record the days late.
Confirm each late lodgement carries a dated Regulatory Affairs Manager sign-off and a documented launch decision.
testing.done: lodgement timing is recomputed for every sampled submission and every late lodgement has a signed-off launch decision.

testing.step: Test objection and supplementary-question handling
actions: Open the SERFF Correspondence tab and the FSA electronic system message history for each sampled filing and list every inbound item with its date.
Compare that list to the filing log entries and record any regulator communication never logged.
For each objection or question, compare the response date to the regulator's stated deadline and record any breach.
Read the response actually sent and confirm it was cleared by the owner named on the anticipated-questions sheet before dispatch.
testing.done: every regulator communication on the sample is logged, answered within its deadline and cleared by the named owner.

testing.step: Trace dispositions to the release gate and to first sale
actions: Take the recorded disposition date and authorized effective date for each sampled authorization filing.
Pull the first policy issued on the affected provision in that jurisdiction from the policy administration platform, with its issue date.
Confirm the first issue date is on or after the authorized effective date, and that the release gate flipped only after the disposition was recorded.
Treat any sale before the authorized effective date as a reportable breach, notify the Head of Compliance the same day, and quantify the policies and premium involved.
testing.done: no sampled jurisdiction sold on the provision before its authorized effective date, and every gate release traces to a recorded disposition.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the filing, the identifier, what failed and the regulatory consequence.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list (lodged outside the process, manifest mismatch, missed objection deadline, disposition not written back, reserve figure not tied, gate released early) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any sale before authorization, open a self-report assessment with General Counsel covering the Art. 128 report and the Art. 315 penalty exposure.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a tracker issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where breach occurred, a self-report assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the thresholds - zero undispatched filings past due, zero unrecorded dispositions beyond 5 business days - and split it by channel.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper reference behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who lodged and tracked none of the sampled submissions and sits outside Regulatory Filing, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any breaches to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper under REG-030.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate by channel and committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Product Operations owns the pre-use release gate and is the only function that can flip a jurisdiction from BLOCKED to RELEASED; General Counsel owns the Art. 107 voting-rights and Art. 271-10 shareholding clearances that gate structural launches

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Insurance Business Act Art. 107 (ceiling of generally 10% of the voting rights of a domestic company outside the permitted categories without FSA approval) and Art. 271-10 with Art. 271-3 (major shareholder approval and notification thresholds), read together with Art. 123 on the pre-use authorization of basic documents, all re-read on e-Gov at gate configuration

In-scope processes.value: Pre-use release control for every product, rider and rate change: blocking sale, quotation, illustration and marketing in a jurisdiction until the FSA authorization or the state approval/deemer is recorded, and blocking any launch dependent on a shareholding that exceeds the Art. 107 voting-rights ceiling until FSA approval is in hand

In-scope systems.value: Product effective-dating and sale-eligibility rules in the policy administration platform, mirrored in the quotation and illustration tools and in the broker portal product catalogue

Compliance procedure documented.value: Pre-Use Release Gate Procedure: gate creation at determination, per-jurisdiction BLOCKED default, evidence required to release (authorization letter, notification receipt, state approval or satisfied deemer computation), Art. 107 / Art. 271-10 structural clearance check, and the four-eyes release approval

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Operating Officer and the Head of Compliance; re-approved annually and after any release-gate incident

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Gate holds until the authorized effective date; for US file-and-use states the deemer date is computed as submission date plus the state's statutory review days and the gate cannot release before it; Art. 107 approvals must be in hand before any shareholding crosses the 10% voting-rights ceiling, not after

Deadline reminders configured.value: Daily blocked-jurisdiction report to Product Operations, alerts on the computed deemer date for every file-and-use state, and a standing alert when any monitored shareholding reaches 8% of voting rights so the Art. 107 approval starts before the ceiling

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Gate configuration history with every state change, the releasing evidence document, the release approver and timestamp, and the Art. 107 / Art. 271-10 clearance memoranda, retained 10 years from product withdrawal

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any sale, quote or illustration produced on a blocked provision, and any shareholding crossing the ceiling without approval, is logged as a breach with policy-count exposure, root cause and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: General Counsel signs off every pre-authorization sale remediation, every self-report decision and every Art. 107 / Art. 271-10 breach disposition

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every policy, quotation and illustration issued in the period on a provision subject to a release gate, plus every gate state change in the gate audit trail, plus every shareholding in a domestic company held at any point in the period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance - one policy issued before the authorized effective date is a fail; one gate released without an attached releasing evidence document is a fail; one shareholding above the Art. 107 ceiling without approval is a fail escalated immediately to the Board Governance Lead and General Counsel

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per filing and continuous in effect; the gate test runs monthly on issued business and quarterly on the full gate audit trail, with the Art. 107 / Art. 271-10 shareholding test run quarterly and at each acquisition

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Product Operations and must not hold release-approval rights in the policy administration platform

Evidence location for test results.value: Monthly pre-use gate workpaper with the issued-business population, the gate audit trail extract and the shareholding test, filed in the compliance evidence repository under REG-030

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Gate audit trail export showing per-jurisdiction blocked and released dates with the releasing evidence attached, plus the Art. 107 approval letters, presentable to an FSA on-site inspection or a market conduct exam within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Affairs Manager handles FSA questions on pre-use sales; General Counsel clears every admission of a sale before authorization and owns the Art. 128 self-report decision

checklist.step: Create the gate at determination with every jurisdiction blocked by default
actions: Take the closed determination from Product Compliance and create a gate record per product change per jurisdiction.
Set every jurisdiction to BLOCKED with no earliest-use date, including jurisdictions classified as notification-only, until the notification receipt exists.
Record on each gate row the classification, the competent authority and the evidence type that will be required to release it.
Confirm the gate record is linked to the determination row and the filing log row so all three move together.
