checklist.done: a gate row exists per jurisdiction, defaulted to BLOCKED, linked to its determination and filing rows.

checklist.step: Enforce the block in the systems that can actually sell
actions: Configure the product effective date and sale-eligibility rule in the policy administration platform so the provision cannot be selected for a risk in a blocked jurisdiction.
Apply the same block in the quotation and illustration tools so no illustration can be produced on the unauthorized basis.
Remove or hide the product from the broker portal catalogue for blocked jurisdictions and confirm the change with the Broker Support Specialist.
Record the configuration change ticket number on the gate row and attach the configuration screenshot.
checklist.done: the block is enforced in policy admin, quotation, illustration and the broker catalogue, with the change ticket recorded on the gate row.

checklist.step: Prove the block works before the filing is even lodged
actions: In the pre-production environment attempt to quote and issue on the blocked provision in each blocked jurisdiction.
Confirm the system refuses the transaction with the expected message and writes an audit entry rather than silently defaulting to the old wording.
Attempt the same through the broker portal and the illustration tool to prove the block is not policy-admin-only.
Record the test evidence with screenshots on the gate row and raise a defect if any channel lets the transaction through.
checklist.done: negative testing evidences a refused transaction in every sales channel for every blocked jurisdiction.

checklist.step: Test the launch for an Art. 107 voting-rights trigger
actions: Ask Corporate Development whether the launch depends on acquiring or increasing a holding in a domestic company - a distribution joint venture, an agency, a technology provider or a fund vehicle.
Where it does, compute the voting rights the company and its subsidiaries would hold in aggregate as a percentage of total voting rights.

Compare the result to the Art. 107 ceiling of generally 10% and confirm whether the target falls into a permitted category (insurance-related or finance-related business) that sits outside the ceiling.
Where the ceiling would be exceeded outside a permitted category, open an FSA approval application and block the launch on that dependency until approval is granted.
Record the analysis, the computed percentage and the conclusion in a dated memorandum on the gate record.
checklist.done: a dated memorandum records the computed voting-rights percentage, the permitted-category test and either a clearance or a blocking approval application.

checklist.step: Test the group side for Art. 271-10 major shareholder thresholds
actions: Pull the current shareholder register and identify any holder approaching or crossing the major shareholder thresholds referenced in Art. 271-10 and Art. 271-3.
Confirm whether any approval or notification obligation sits with the shareholder, with the company, or both, and who is lodging it.
Where a group restructuring accompanies the launch, confirm the holding company approval position before the launch date.
Report the position to the Board Governance Lead and record it on the gate record with the date checked.
checklist.done: the shareholder position against the Art. 271-10 thresholds is documented, with the lodging party identified and reported to the board.

checklist.step: Compute and record the deemer date for every file-and-use jurisdiction
actions: Take the state's statutory review period from the dated SERFF filing-rules capture made at determination.
Compute deemer date = submission date plus review days, counting the way the state counts (calendar or business days) and excluding any period the filing sat suspended for objection.
Write the computed deemer date and the counting convention onto the gate row, with the captured instructions page as the support.
Reset the deemer computation every time an objection stops the clock and record each reset.
checklist.done: each file-and-use jurisdiction carries a computed deemer date, its counting convention, its supporting capture and every clock reset.

checklist.step: Define exactly what evidence releases each gate row
actions: For Art. 123(1) rows require the FSA authorization letter naming the authorized effective date.
For Art. 123(2) rows require the dated notification receipt from the FSA electronic system.

For US prior-approval rows require the state approval letter or the SERFF disposition of Approved/Filed; for file-and-use rows require the submission receipt plus the elapsed computed deemer date with no objection outstanding.
Write the required evidence type onto every gate row so no releaser has to make a judgement call at release time.
checklist.done: every gate row names its single required releasing evidence type with no ambiguity left to the releaser.

checklist.step: Release a gate row only on four eyes and attached evidence
actions: Open the gate row, attach the required evidence document and enter the authorized or deemed effective date exactly as it appears on the evidence.
Submit the release for second approval by the Compliance Manager - the system must not permit the preparer to approve their own release.
On approval set the jurisdiction to RELEASED with the earliest-use date, and leave every other jurisdiction untouched.
Confirm the policy administration effective date, the quotation tool and the broker catalogue all move to the same date, and re-test one quote in that jurisdiction.
checklist.done: each release carries attached evidence, a distinct preparer and approver, an earliest-use date matching the evidence, and a post-release quote test.

checklist.step: Carry regulator conditions into the launch before first sale
actions: List every condition or undertaking attached to the authorization or state approval - suitability standards, disclosure wording, channel restrictions, reporting commitments.
Assign each condition to an owning function with a due date that precedes the earliest-use date.
Verify each condition is actually implemented (training delivered, disclosure inserted, channel restriction configured) before the gate release is confirmed.
Record the verification evidence against the gate row.
checklist.done: every regulator condition is owned, implemented and evidenced before first sale in that jurisdiction.

checklist.step: Run the daily blocked-jurisdiction report
actions: Run the daily report of blocked jurisdictions against issued business, quotes and illustrations for the previous day.
Investigate any hit the same day - a hit means the block was bypassed or a channel was missed at configuration.
Suspend sale of the affected provision in that jurisdiction immediately while the cause is established.
Escalate every confirmed hit to the Head of Compliance and General Counsel within one business day.
checklist.done: the daily report runs, every hit is investigated the same day and confirmed hits are suspended and escalated within one business day.

checklist.step: Handle a disapproval or a withdrawal without touching the gate
actions: On a disapproval, confirm the gate row stays BLOCKED and record the regulator's stated reason on it verbatim.
Decide and record the response: amend and refile, drop the jurisdiction from the launch, or launch on the currently authorized wording.
Where the product has already launched elsewhere, confirm nothing about the disapproved jurisdiction was configured in advance.
Notify Distribution in writing that the jurisdiction is out and confirm the broker catalogue reflects it.
checklist.done: the disapproved jurisdiction remains blocked with a recorded reason, a recorded decision and a confirmed catalogue removal.

checklist.step: Reconcile the gate to the filing log weekly
actions: Export the gate rows and the filing log rows and match them on determination id and jurisdiction.
List gate rows released with no corresponding disposition on the filing log, and dispositions recorded with the gate still blocked more than 5 business days later.
Investigate both directions - an early release is a breach risk, a late release is a lost revenue and a control signal.
Sign the reconciliation and file it with the week's evidence.
checklist.done: gate rows and filing dispositions reconcile weekly with both early and late releases investigated and the reconciliation signed.

checklist.step: Monitor the shareholding position against the Art. 107 ceiling continuously
actions: Refresh the register of holdings in domestic companies monthly, showing voting rights held by the company and each subsidiary and the aggregate percentage.
Trigger a review at 8% aggregate voting rights so an Art. 107 approval application can be prepared before the 10% ceiling is reached.
Flag any passive increase - buybacks by the investee, dilution reversals - that could push the aggregate above the ceiling without a purchase.
Report the register and any trigger to General Counsel and the Chief Investment Officer monthly.
checklist.done: a monthly holdings register with aggregate voting-rights percentages is reported, with an 8% trigger operating ahead of the ceiling.

checklist.step: Close the gate record when the launch completes
actions: Close the gate record only when every jurisdiction is either RELEASED with evidence or formally out of the launch with a recorded decision.
Confirm no jurisdiction is left in an indefinite BLOCKED state with no owner or decision.
Attach the final gate audit trail export to the product change record.
Hand the closed gate record to Records for archival.
checklist.done: the gate record closes with every jurisdiction either evidenced-released or formally excluded, and the audit trail attached.

checklist.step: Archive the gate audit trail and clearance memoranda
actions: Move the gate audit trail, the releasing evidence documents, the four-eyes approval records and the Art. 107 / Art. 271-10 memoranda into the compliance evidence repository under REG-030 and the product code.
Apply the 10-years-from-product-withdrawal retention label and mark the record inspection-relevant.
Index by product code, jurisdiction, authorized effective date and release approver.
Write the archive reference back to the gate record and the determination row.
checklist.done: the gate audit trail and clearance memoranda are archived under a 10-year label and indexed by jurisdiction and effective date.

testing.step: Build the population of business issued on gated provisions
actions: Extract every policy, endorsement, quotation and illustration issued in the period on a provision carrying a release gate, with jurisdiction and issue timestamp.
Add in-force conversions and rider additions so an unauthorized provision cannot enter through servicing rather than new business.
Reconcile the extract to the new-business production report for the period and resolve every difference before sampling.
Sign the population as complete and record the extraction query in the workpaper.
testing.done: the issued-business population reconciles to the production report and is signed complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every issue to a gate that was open at the issue date
actions: Match each population row to its gate row on product change id and jurisdiction.
Compare the issue timestamp to the gate's earliest-use date and to the gate state change history at that moment.
List every issue that pre-dates its jurisdiction's earliest-use date, or that occurred while the gate audit trail shows BLOCKED, as an automatic breach.
Quantify each breach: policy count, premium, and whether the policyholder was charged on an unauthorized basis.
testing.done: every issued row is matched to an open gate at the issue moment, or listed as a quantified breach.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of gate releases
actions: Take 100% of releases on Art. 123(1) authorization rows and 100% of releases on file-and-use deemer rows.
Take 20 further releases by seeded random selection from the remainder, minimum total 35 releases.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date so the sample is redrawable.
Confirm the sample includes at least one disapproved jurisdiction and one jurisdiction dropped from the launch.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all authorization and deemer releases plus adverse outcomes is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the release decision against the attached evidence
actions: Open the evidence document attached to each sampled release and read the effective date off it yourself before looking at the gate row.
Compare your date to the earliest-use date recorded on the gate and treat any difference as an exception, including a release dated to the disposition date rather than the authorized effective date.
Confirm the evidence type matches the type the gate row required - a notification receipt cannot release an authorization row.
Capture the evidence document and your recomputed date into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled release has an independently read effective date matching the gate, on the correct evidence type.

testing.step: Recompute the deemer maths on file-and-use releases
actions: For each sampled file-and-use release open the SERFF filing and take the submission date and the objection history.
Recompute deemer date = submission date plus the state's statutory review days using the state's counting convention, adding back any period the clock was suspended for an objection.
Compare to the earliest-use date on the gate and record any release made before the recomputed deemer date as a breach.
Capture the SERFF filing detail and objection history into the workpaper.
testing.done: deemer dates are independently recomputed with objection suspensions applied, and every early release is recorded as a breach.

testing.step: Test the four-eyes control on releases
actions: Extract the gate audit trail showing preparer and approver identity and timestamp for every release in the period.
List any release where preparer and approver are the same person, or where the approver holds a Product Operations preparer role.
Attempt a self-approval in the pre-production environment to confirm the system enforces the segregation rather than relying on procedure.
Record any release approved outside the authorised approver list as an exception.
testing.done: every release shows distinct preparer and approver, and system enforcement of segregation is evidenced by test.

testing.step: Test the Art. 107 voting-rights position independently
actions: Obtain the holdings register for every domestic company in which the group held voting rights at any point in the period.
Recompute the aggregate voting-rights percentage for the company and its subsidiaries at each month end from the underlying share counts, not from the register's own percentage.
Compare each recomputed figure to the 10% ceiling and check whether any target outside a permitted category exceeded it without an FSA approval on file.
Confirm the 8% trigger fired where it should have and that an approval application followed within the stated lead time.
testing.done: aggregate voting rights are independently recomputed at each month end and every ceiling approach or breach is evidenced against an approval.

testing.step: Test the channel-level blocks by attempted transaction
actions: Pick five currently blocked jurisdictions and attempt, in pre-production, to quote, illustrate and issue on the blocked provision through policy admin, the illustration tool and the broker portal.
Record for each attempt whether the transaction was refused and whether an audit entry was written.
Where any channel permits the transaction, quantify how long that channel has been open by comparing the configuration change date to the gate creation date.
Capture the refusal or success screenshots into the workpaper.
testing.done: every tested channel refuses the blocked transaction with an audit entry, or the open window is quantified as an exception.

testing.step: Log breaches and exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per breach naming the product, jurisdiction, policy count, premium and the provision sold without authorization.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list (gate never created, channel not configured, released on wrong evidence, deemer miscomputed, self-approval, ceiling breach) and an owner.
Set a remediation date, decide with General Counsel whether policyholder remediation and an Art. 128 self-report are required, and record the decision.
Carry every open breach into the next monthly test as a mandatory retest row until it is closed and retested clean.
testing.done: every breach has a tracker issue, quantified exposure, root cause, owner, remediation date and a self-report decision.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: State the count of pre-authorization sales and ceiling breaches against the zero-tolerance threshold, with the premium exposure attached.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper reference behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Product Operations and holds no release-approval rights, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee and, for any ceiling breach, to the Board Governance Lead, and file the signed workpaper under REG-030.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the breach count and exposure, and the committee and board reporting dates.

Accountable obligation owner.value: IT / Product owns the build that puts the authorized wording and premium basis into policy admin and rating; the Product / Filing Actuary owns confirmation that what was built equals what was authorized

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Insurance Business Act Art. 123 (amendments to the statement of business procedures, general policy conditions and premium/policy-reserve calculation methods require prior FSA authorization) with Art. 125 on the notification route, and Art. 5(1) on the documents attached at licensing that the basic documents descend from; the authorized text used for the build is the version attached to the FSA authorization letter, not the as-lodged draft

In-scope processes.value: Implementation of authorized basic-document changes into the policy administration system, the rating and pricing engine, the illustration and quotation tools, the printed and electronic policy document templates and the broker portal catalogue, effective-dated to the authorized effective date

In-scope systems.value: Policy administration product model and wording templates, with the premium basis configured in the rating and pricing engine and the change shipped through the standard release pipeline

Compliance procedure documented.value: Authorized Change Implementation Procedure: build only from the authorization-attached text, clause-to-configuration traceability matrix, effective-dating rule, regression on the prior authorized version, four-eyes configuration review and a post-deployment first-policy verification

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Information Officer and the Head of Compliance; re-approved annually and after any implementation defect that reached production

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Build complete and regression-passed before the authorized effective date; deployment scheduled so the configuration goes live on that date and not before; in-force conversion dated per the transitional treatment stated in the authorized statement of reasons

Deadline reminders configured.value: Release pipeline milestones at T-15 (build complete), T-10 (regression passed), T-5 (change advisory approval) and T-0 (authorized effective date) business days, alerting the Release Coordinator and the Product / Filing Actuary

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Traceability matrix, configuration diff, test evidence, deployment record, and the first-policy verification pack retained 10 years from withdrawal of the implemented provision

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any configuration that differs from the authorized text, deploys before the authorized effective date, or misses a channel is raised as a P1 compliance defect with policy-count impact and a remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Chief Actuary signs off any correction to an implemented premium basis or reserve-relevant configuration; Regulatory Counsel signs off any wording correction and whether a re-notification under Art. 125 is required

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every release that changed a product-model, wording-template or rating-engine artefact in the period, and every policy issued on a changed provision in its first month of use

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Fail if the deployed wording differs in substance from the authorization-attached text, if any rated premium differs from the authorized basis by more than 0.01% or one currency unit, if the deployment date precedes the authorized effective date, or if any sales channel still runs the superseded version after go-live

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per filing; the test runs per release for authorized changes and monthly across all releases, with 100% re-performance on premium-basis and guarantee-charge changes

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have configured, tested or deployed the sampled change and must hold no write access to the product model

Evidence location for test results.value: Per-release implementation verification pack (traceability matrix, diff, recalculation results, first-policy evidence) attached to the release record and copied into the compliance evidence repository under REG-030

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Authorization letter, authorized text, traceability matrix, configuration diff and issued specimen policy showing the authorized wording and premium, producible for an FSA inspection or a market conduct exam within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Affairs Manager answers FSA questions about implemented wording; the Product / Filing Actuary supplies the premium recalculation; General Counsel clears any admission that policies were issued on non-authorized text

checklist.step: Take the authorized text as the single build input
actions: Download the FSA authorization letter and the text attached to it, or the state approval and the SERFF-approved form version, from the filing record.
Compare that text against the as-lodged package and highlight any regulator-driven amendment made during review.
Publish the authorized version into the Basic Document Register as the current authorized wording with its authorization number and effective date.
Issue the authorized text to IT / Product as the only permitted build input and state in writing that drafts must not be used.
checklist.done: the authorization-attached text is registered as the current authorized version and issued as the sole build input.

checklist.step: Build the clause-to-configuration traceability matrix
actions: List every authorized clause and calculation-method element that changed, with its clause number and effective date.
Map each one to the concrete configuration artefact that will carry it: product-model field, coverage term, eligibility rule, rating table, wording template paragraph, illustration label.
Mark any authorized element with no mapped artefact as a build gap and resolve it before development starts.
Have the Product / Filing Actuary review and sign the matrix before any configuration is cut.
checklist.done: every authorized element maps to a named configuration artefact on a matrix signed by the filing actuary.

checklist.step: Configure the product model and wording templates
actions: In the policy administration product model create a new effective-dated version of the product rather than editing the live version in place.
Set the version effective date to the authorized effective date and confirm the prior version remains addressable for in-force policies.
Update the wording templates paragraph by paragraph from the authorized text, using copy from the authorized document rather than retyping.
Update the eligibility, underwriting-limit and sales-area rules that flow from the statement of business procedures.
Record the configuration change id against each matrix row.
checklist.done: a new effective-dated product version carries the authorized wording and rules, with configuration ids written back to the matrix.

checklist.step: Configure the premium basis in the rating engine
actions: Load the authorized rate tables, factors and the guarantee charge for the Variable Annuity into a new effective-dated rating version.
Check every table against the authorized statement of calculation methods cell by cell, including the rounding rule and the minimum premium.
Configure the effective-date rule so quotes dated before the authorized effective date still rate on the prior authorized version.
Produce a rating specification document that names the source exhibit page for each loaded table and file it with the release.
checklist.done: the rating version carries the authorized tables and rounding rules, cell-checked against the authorized calculation method statement.

checklist.step: Update the downstream channels that also present the product
actions: List every downstream consumer: illustration tool, quotation tool, broker portal catalogue, customer self-service portal, call-centre desktop, printed and electronic policy pack.
Raise a configuration task per channel with the same effective date and the same authorized text extract.
Confirm with each channel owner in writing that the change is scheduled for the same release, and escalate any channel that cannot make the date.
Record channel readiness on the release record - a channel left behind sells the superseded wording.
checklist.done: every downstream channel has an owned, scheduled configuration task with confirmed readiness for the same effective date.

checklist.step: Test the rated premium against the authorized basis
actions: Build a test pack of at least 30 representative risks spanning age bands, sums assured, riders, guarantee options and payment frequencies.
Compute the expected premium for each independently from the authorized rate tables in a spreadsheet, not from the system.
Run the same risks through the configured rating engine and compare, requiring agreement to the last currency unit.
Investigate every difference to root cause - a rounding rule mismatch is a defect, not a tolerance - and re-test after fix.
Sign the recalculation pack and attach it to the release record.
checklist.done: at least 30 test risks rate to the authorized premium to the last currency unit, evidenced in a signed recalculation pack.

checklist.step: Test the produced documents against the authorized wording
actions: Issue specimen policies in the test environment for each variant and generate the full document pack.
Diff the produced wording against the authorized text paragraph by paragraph using a text comparison tool, not by eye.
Check clause numbering, defined terms, cross-references, the fund menu on the Variable Annuity and the disclosure inserts required by any authorization condition.
Log every difference as a defect and require a clean diff before sign-off.
checklist.done: a clean paragraph-level diff exists between the produced document pack and the authorized text for every variant.

checklist.step: Regression-test the prior authorized version and the in-force book
actions: Re-run the existing regression suite on the prior product version to prove in-force policies still rate, renew and produce documents on the wording authorized for them.
Test mid-term adjustments, renewals and claims on in-force contracts across the effective-date boundary.
Test the transitional treatment stated in the authorized statement of reasons - whether in-force contracts move to the new wording or stay on the old.
Record pass/fail per suite and block the release on any failure touching in-force contracts.
checklist.done: regression proves in-force contracts remain on their authorized wording and the stated transitional treatment behaves as filed.

checklist.step: Review the configuration on four eyes before release
actions: Open the configuration diff between the prior and the new product and rating versions in the repository pull request.
Walk the diff against the traceability matrix and confirm every change maps to an authorized element and nothing else was changed alongside it.
Reject the pull request if it bundles unrelated changes with the authorized change - regulated changes ship alone.
Approve with a named reviewer who did not author the configuration and record the approval on the release record.
checklist.done: the configuration diff is reviewed against the matrix by a second named engineer with no unrelated changes bundled.

checklist.step: Schedule deployment to land on the authorized effective date
actions: Raise the change request with the authorization number, the authorized effective date and the release gate evidence attached.

Schedule the deployment so the configuration becomes effective on the authorized effective date - deploy earlier only if the effective-dating genuinely prevents use before that date, and evidence that.
Confirm the change advisory board approval references the release gate status as RELEASED for the jurisdiction.
Publish the deployment plan and the back-out plan to Product Operations and Distribution.
checklist.done: an approved change request ties the deployment to the authorization number and the authorized effective date with a back-out plan.

checklist.step: Deploy and verify the first live transaction
actions: Deploy the product and rating versions and confirm the effective dates read correctly in production configuration.
Produce one controlled live quote and one live specimen policy in the jurisdiction on the effective date.
Check the premium against the authorized basis and diff the produced wording against the authorized text before general availability.
Only then open the product to the channels, and record the verification pack on the release record.
checklist.done: a first live quote and policy are verified against the authorized premium and wording before general availability.

checklist.step: Confirm every channel is actually serving the new version
actions: On the effective date, check each channel in turn - broker portal, illustration tool, self-service portal, call-centre desktop - and confirm it presents the new version.
Produce one artefact from each channel and compare it to the authorized text.
Where any channel still serves the superseded version, suspend sale in that channel and escalate the same day.
Record the channel confirmation evidence on the release record.
checklist.done: each sales channel is evidenced serving the authorized version on the effective date, or is suspended and escalated.

checklist.step: Monitor the first month of issued business on the new version
actions: Build a daily report over policies issued on the new product version showing rated premium, wording version and jurisdiction.
Recompute the premium for a daily sample of 10 policies against the authorized tables and report any mismatch immediately.
Watch for policies issued on the superseded version after the effective date and for any issued on the new version before it.
Report the first-month results to the Product / Filing Actuary and close the monitoring only when a clean week is achieved.
checklist.done: a month of daily premium and wording-version monitoring is complete with a clean closing week and any mismatch escalated.

checklist.step: Handle an implementation difference from the authorized text
actions: On any confirmed difference between the deployed configuration and the authorized text, quantify the affected policies and the policyholder impact with the Product / Filing Actuary.
Decide whether the difference is a system defect to correct or a substantive divergence requiring a fresh Art. 123 authorization or an Art. 125 notification.
Where policyholders were charged or covered on a non-authorized basis, agree the remediation - repricing, endorsement or refund - and the customer communication.
Record the decision, the FSA notification position and the remediation owner on the defect record.
checklist.done: every deployed-versus-authorized difference has a quantified impact, a filing decision and an owned policyholder remediation.

checklist.step: Archive the implementation evidence against the authorization
actions: Move the traceability matrix, configuration diff, recalculation pack, document diffs, deployment record and first-live verification into the compliance evidence repository under REG-030 and the product code.
Apply the 10-years-from-provision-withdrawal retention label and link the record to the authorization number.
Index by product code, product version, rating version, authorization number and effective date.
Write the archive reference back to the release record and the Basic Document Register entry.
checklist.done: the implementation evidence is archived against the authorization number under a 10-year label and indexed by product and rating version.

testing.step: Build the population of regulated configuration changes
actions: Extract every release in the period that touched a product-model, wording-template, rating-table or illustration artefact, with its change request and deployment timestamp.
Add rating-engine table loads made outside the release pipeline so out-of-band changes cannot hide.
Reconcile the extract to the Basic Document Register entries created in the period and resolve every difference.
Sign the population as complete and record the extraction query and date.
testing.done: the configuration-change population reconciles to the register and is signed complete, including out-of-band table loads.

testing.step: Reconcile each configuration change to an authorization
actions: Match each population row to an authorization number or notification receipt in the Basic Document Register.
Confirm the authorization date pre-dates the deployment and that the configuration effective date equals the authorized effective date.
List changes with no authorization, or deployed before authorization, as automatic breaches.
Quantify each breach: policies issued on the unauthorized configuration and the premium involved.
testing.done: every configuration change is matched to a pre-dated authorization or listed as a quantified breach.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of changes touching the premium basis, the guarantee charge or the policy reserve method.
Take 15 further changes by seeded random selection from the remainder, minimum total 25.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date so the sample can be redrawn.
Confirm the sample includes at least one Variable Annuity change and one in-force-affecting change.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all premium-basis and guarantee changes is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the wording diff against the authorized text
actions: Pull the authorization-attached text from the filing archive, not from the Basic Document Register, so a corrupted register entry is detectable.
Generate a specimen document pack from the production configuration for the sampled variant.
Run your own paragraph-level text diff and record every substantive difference, ignoring only formatting.
Capture the diff output into the workpaper as the evidence.
testing.done: an independently produced diff between production output and the authorization-attached text is captured for each sampled change.

testing.step: Recalculate premiums independently from the authorized tables
actions: Select 15 issued policies per sampled change spanning the rating dimensions, and take their risk characteristics from the policy record.
Compute the premium from the authorized rate tables and the authorized rounding rule by hand or in an independent spreadsheet.
Compare to the premium actually charged and record any difference above one currency unit as an exception with the policy count extrapolated to the book.
Confirm the guarantee charge on Variable Annuity policies matches the authorized charge basis exactly.
testing.done: premiums on sampled issued policies reproduce from the authorized tables to the last currency unit, or the exception is extrapolated.

testing.step: Test the effective-dating boundary on issued business
actions: Extract policies issued in the five business days either side of each sampled authorized effective date, with the product and rating version applied.
Confirm policies dated before the effective date carry the prior authorized version and those on or after carry the new one.
Investigate any policy on the new version before the effective date as a pre-authorization sale and any on the old version after it as an unimplemented change.
Capture the version-by-issue-date extract into the workpaper.
testing.done: the version applied on each side of the effective-date boundary is correct for every sampled change, or the exception is investigated.

testing.step: Test change control and segregation on the deployments
actions: Pull the change request for each sampled deployment and confirm it names the authorization number and carries change advisory approval before the deployment timestamp.
Confirm the configuration pull request has a reviewer distinct from the author and that no unrelated change was bundled with the regulated change.
Check who holds production write access to the product model and rating tables and whether any deployer also approved their own change.
Record any deployment made without an approved change request as an exception with the artefacts touched.
testing.done: every sampled deployment has a pre-dated approved change request, a distinct reviewer and no bundled unrelated changes.

testing.step: Verify every channel is on the authorized version today
actions: For each sampled change, produce a live artefact from each channel - broker portal quote, illustration, self-service document, call-centre quote.
Diff each artefact against the authorized text and premium basis.
Record any channel still serving the superseded version, with the date it should have changed and the volume transacted since.
Capture each artefact into the workpaper.
testing.done: every channel is evidenced serving the authorized version, or the stale channel and its transacted volume are recorded.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a defect per exception naming the product, version, artefact and the policies affected.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list (built from draft text, table transcription error, rounding rule mismatch, channel missed, deployed early, unrelated change bundled) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, with Regulatory Counsel, decide whether a fresh authorization or notification and a policyholder remediation are required.
Carry every open defect into the next monthly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a defect record, root cause, owner, remediation date and a filing and policyholder remediation decision.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: State the premium recalculation match rate, the wording diff result and the count of unauthorized or early deployments against the thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper reference behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who configured, tested and deployed none of the sampled changes and holds no product-model write access, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-030.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the match rate and the unauthorized-deployment count, with the committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: The filing analyst owns every objection and supplementary question from receipt to closure; the Chief Investment Officer owns the substance of any answer touching the Art. 115 price fluctuation reserve rates, ceiling or drawdown

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Insurance Business Act Art. 115 (price fluctuation reserve accumulation at FSA-set rates and drawdown restricted to realised losses beyond the prescribed threshold), Art. 116 and Art. 117, re-read with the current Ordinance for Enforcement rate table before any answer citing reserve treatment is sent

In-scope processes.value: Receipt, triage, drafting, clearance and lodgement of responses to FSA supplementary questions on basic-document applications and to state objection letters and interrogatories in SERFF, including questions on the price fluctuation reserve accrual, its ceiling and any drawdown

In-scope systems.value: Objection register with per-item due dates in the filing tracker, drafted in the Internal Regulatory System and lodged through SERFF Correspondence or the FSA Electronic Application and Notification System

Compliance procedure documented.value: Objection and Supplementary Question Response Procedure: same-day logging, deadline computation from the regulator's stated period, answer-owner assignment by subject (reserves, wording, pricing, distribution), evidence attachment rule, clearance chain and lodgement with receipt capture

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Regulatory Affairs Manager and the Head of Compliance; re-approved annually and after any missed response deadline

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Event-driven - each objection carries the regulator's own deadline (commonly 10 to 30 days on a state objection letter, and the date stated in an FSA supplementary question); the internal draft deadline is set 5 business days ahead of it, and an extension must be requested in writing before the original date passes

Deadline reminders configured.value: Tracker alerts on receipt day, at the internal draft deadline, at 3 business days before the regulator deadline and daily thereafter until lodged; an unanswered item inside 3 days auto-escalates to the Regulatory Affairs Manager

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Objection letter or question as received, the drafting thread, the cleared answer, every attachment lodged with it and the lodgement receipt, retained 10 years from the disposition of the parent filing

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A response lodged after the regulator deadline, an unrequested extension, an answer sent without the required clearance, or a filing closed by the regulator for non-response is logged as an exception with root cause and remediation

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Regulatory Affairs Manager signs off every late response, every extension request and every re-answer after a regulator rejects a first response

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every objection letter, interrogatory and supplementary question received in the period, taken from the SERFF Correspondence tabs and the FSA electronic system message history rather than from the internal register

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on missed regulator deadlines; fail if a response was lodged after the stated deadline without a pre-agreed extension, if a reserve-related answer went out without Chief Investment Officer or Chief Actuary clearance, or if any received item was never logged

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven; the test runs monthly over that month's received objections, with 100% coverage of items answered late and of every answer touching the Art. 115 reserve

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have drafted or lodged any sampled response and must sit outside Regulatory Filing

Evidence location for test results.value: Monthly objection-handling workpaper with the regulator-side item list, the register reconciliation, the timeliness recomputation and the clearance test, filed in the compliance evidence repository under REG-030

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Objection register export showing each item, its stated deadline, the response date and the lodged answer with attachments, producible for an FSA inspection or a market conduct exam within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: All correspondence leaves through the Regulatory Affairs Manager for FSA items and the named SERFF filing contact for state items; the Chief Actuary clears reserve answers and Regulatory Counsel clears anything conceding a wording or compliance point

checklist.step: Sweep the regulator channels for new items every business day
actions: Open the SERFF Correspondence tab on every open filing and the Objection Letter list, and download anything received since the last sweep.
Check the FSA Electronic Application and Notification System message history and the regulatory affairs mailbox for supplementary questions and telephone-note follow-ups.
Download each item as a PDF named <filing id>-objection-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf and store it against the filing record.
Record the sweep as completed each day even when nothing was received, so a silent gap is visible.
checklist.done: a dated daily sweep record exists for every channel and every received item is downloaded against its filing.

checklist.step: Log each item and compute its response deadline the day it arrives
actions: Create an objection register entry with filing id, jurisdiction, regulator reviewer name, receipt date and the item type (objection letter, interrogatory, supplementary question, request to amend).
Read the deadline the regulator states and record it verbatim, together with whether it counts in calendar or business days.
Compute the internal draft deadline as the regulator deadline minus 5 business days and set the tracker alerts.
Split a multi-part objection into one register row per numbered question so no sub-question is lost inside a bundle.
checklist.done: every received item is logged the same day, split per numbered question, with the regulator deadline recorded verbatim and alerts set.

checklist.step: Assign each question to the answer owner by subject
actions: Route reserve and solvency questions - price fluctuation reserve rates, ceiling, drawdown, policy reserve basis - to the Chief Investment Officer or the Appointed Actuary as applicable.
Route wording and policyholder-protection questions to Regulatory Counsel, pricing questions to the Pricing Actuary, and distribution and suitability questions to Market Conduct.
Notify each owner the same day with the question text, the deadline and the internal draft date, and record their acceptance.
Where a question spans subjects, name one lead owner rather than leaving it jointly owned.
checklist.done: every register row has one named answer owner who has accepted it, with the deadline communicated the day of receipt.

checklist.step: Reconstruct the position the regulator is questioning
actions: Pull the exact page and paragraph of the lodged package the question refers to, from the frozen version rather than a working draft.
Pull the determination row and the authorized text of the provision as it stood before the amendment.
Assemble a short background note for the answer owner: what was filed, why, and what the regulator has asked.
Flag whether the question implies the regulator has read a different version from the one lodged, which would point to a lodgement defect.
checklist.done: each answer owner receives a background note tied to the frozen lodged page and the pre-amendment authorized text.

checklist.step: Answer a price fluctuation reserve question from the current rate table
actions: Re-read the Ordinance for Enforcement accumulation-rate table in force at the valuation date rather than relying on the figure already filed.
Rebuild the computation from the platform position report: book value by asset class, the rate applied, the resulting accrual and the accumulated balance against the statutory ceiling.
Where the question concerns a drawdown, set out the realised losses, the prescribed threshold under Art. 115(2) and the amount drawn, and state whether any other use required FSA approval.
Write the answer as a numbered response mirroring the regulator's numbering, with the computation attached as a schedule.
Sign the schedule and pass it to the Chief Actuary for clearance.
checklist.done: the reserve answer is rebuilt from the current rate table and platform positions, numbered to match the question and signed with its schedule.

checklist.step: Draft the response document
actions: Restate each regulator question verbatim above its answer and keep the regulator's numbering throughout.
Answer the question actually asked in the first sentence, then give the support - do not open with background.
Name every attachment inline where it is relied on, and list the attachments at the end with their document ids.
Where the answer concedes a change to the filed wording or basis, mark it clearly and flag it to Regulatory Counsel as a package amendment rather than burying it.
Circulate the draft to the answer owners for confirmation their words survived editing.
checklist.done: a numbered response mirroring the regulator's questions exists, with attachments named inline and any conceded change flagged.

checklist.step: Clear the response through the required chain before it leaves
actions: Confirm the response contains no admission of a compliance failure that has not been assessed for Art. 128 reporting.
Confirm reserve answers carry Chief Actuary clearance and pricing answers carry Head of Pricing clearance, evidenced in writing.
Check every citation in the response against the current statutory text and correct any stale article or ordinance reference.
Record the clearance chain with names, dates and any condition, and only then release the response for lodgement.
checklist.done: the response carries a recorded clearance chain with counsel confirmation that citations are current and no unassessed admission is made.

checklist.step: Lodge the response and capture the receipt
actions: In SERFF open the objection letter and use Respond to Objection Letter, attaching the response and every schedule against the correct document types.
For FSA items lodge through the Electronic Application and Notification System against the original application number, or by the route the case officer specified.
Submit and download the lodgement receipt showing date, time and the documents transmitted.
Record the lodgement date, receipt reference and the elapsed days against the deadline on the register row.
checklist.done: the response is lodged through the regulator's own channel with a captured receipt recorded on the register row.

checklist.step: Request an extension in writing before the deadline, never after
actions: Where the internal draft deadline passes with the answer incomplete, decide by that day whether an extension is needed.
Request the extension through the same channel as the objection, stating the reason, the additional days sought and the new date offered.
Record the request, the regulator's reply and the revised deadline on the register row, and reset the tracker alerts to the new date.
Treat an unanswered extension request as refused and work to the original deadline.
checklist.done: any extension is requested in writing before the original deadline with the regulator's reply and revised date recorded.

checklist.step: Update the package and the determination where the answer changes the filing
actions: Where the response amends filed wording, rates or reserve basis, create a new frozen package version and manifest rather than editing the lodged one.
Update the determination row and the traceability that Product and IT will build from, so nobody builds the superseded text.
Recompute the latest application date and the expected disposition date if the amendment restarts or extends the regulator's clock.
Notify the Insurance Product Manager and the release gate owner of any change to the expected effective date.
checklist.done: any amendment produces a new frozen package version with the determination, build inputs and expected effective date updated.

checklist.step: Track the item to regulator closure, not to lodgement
actions: Keep the register row open after lodgement until the regulator either issues a disposition or confirms the objection satisfied.
Check the SERFF filing status and the FSA message history weekly for a follow-up objection on the same point.
Where a second objection repeats the first, escalate to the Regulatory Affairs Manager - the answer did not land and repeating it will not help.
Close the row only against evidence of regulator acceptance, and record that evidence.
checklist.done: register rows close only against evidenced regulator acceptance, and repeat objections are escalated rather than re-answered.

checklist.step: Run the weekly open-objection review
actions: Run the open-objection report showing days to deadline, answer owner and draft status for every open item.
Escalate any item inside 3 business days of its deadline without a cleared draft to the answer owner's manager the same day.
Review any item where the same answer owner has more than three open questions - that is a capacity failure that will produce a miss.
Record the review, the escalations and the outcomes in the meeting note.
checklist.done: a weekly review record shows every open item's status with escalations raised on anything inside 3 days of deadline.

checklist.step: Feed recurring objection themes back into the package standard
actions: Quarterly, group the period's objections by theme - reserve basis explanation, in-force treatment, guarantee charge justification, readability, missing certification.
For any theme appearing three or more times, add the required content to the JP-116/117 mandatory contents list so the next package pre-empts it.
Update the anticipated-questions sheet template with the strongest answers actually accepted by the regulator.
Report the themes and the standard change to the Compliance Committee.
checklist.done: recurring objection themes are quantified quarterly and folded into the package standard and the anticipated-questions template.

checklist.step: Archive the objection thread with its parent filing
actions: Move the objection as received, the drafting thread, the clearance record, the lodged response, its attachments and the receipt into the compliance evidence repository under the parent filing.
Apply the 10-years-from-parent-disposition retention label and mark the record inspection-relevant.
Index by filing id, application or SERFF tracking number, regulator reviewer and receipt date.
Write the archive reference back to the register row.
checklist.done: each objection thread is archived with its parent filing under a 10-year label and indexed by filing and receipt date.

testing.step: Build the population from the regulator systems
actions: Export every objection letter and note-to-filer from the SERFF Correspondence tabs of all filings open at any point in the period.
Export the FSA Electronic Application and Notification System message history for the same period and entity.
Build the population from those exports, deliberately not from the internal objection register, so unlogged items are in scope.
Sign the population as complete and record both export dates and parameters.
testing.done: the population is built from regulator-side exports and signed complete independently of the internal register.

testing.step: Reconcile the regulator population to the objection register
actions: Match each regulator item to a register row on filing id and receipt date, at the level of the individual numbered question.
List items present in the regulator system with no register row as automatic exceptions and establish how long they went unlogged.
List register rows with no regulator counterpart and establish whether they were invented, duplicated or received by a channel outside the sweep.
Quantify the exposure of unlogged items: whether the deadline passed and whether the filing was closed for non-response.
testing.done: every regulator item matches a register row at question level or is an exception with its unlogged duration quantified.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of items answered after the regulator deadline, 100% of items whose answers touched the Art. 115 price fluctuation reserve, and 100% of filings closed or withdrawn following an objection.
Take 20 further items by seeded random selection from the remainder, minimum total 35.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date so the sample can be redrawn.
Confirm coverage of both SERFF and FSA channels and of at least three distinct answer owners.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all late, reserve-related and adverse-outcome items is documented.

testing.step: Recompute the response deadline and the elapsed days
actions: Read the deadline from the objection letter itself for each sampled item, not from the register, and note the counting convention it uses.
Recompute the due date from the receipt date and compare it to the recorded deadline; a wrongly recorded deadline is an exception even where the answer was timely.
Compare the lodgement receipt timestamp to the recomputed due date and record the days early or late.
Where an extension was claimed, confirm it was requested before the original date and granted in writing.
testing.done: every sampled item has an independently recomputed deadline and a days-early-or-late figure evidenced from the receipt.

testing.step: Re-perform the price fluctuation reserve answer
actions: Pull the position report at the valuation date used in the sampled answer and the Ordinance for Enforcement rate table in force then.
Recompute the accrual by asset class and the accumulated balance, and compare to the schedule sent to the regulator.
Where a drawdown was described, verify the realised losses exceeded the prescribed Art. 115(2) threshold and that the amount drawn matches the schedule.
Record any difference as an exception and assess whether the regulator was given an incorrect figure.
testing.done: the reserve figures sent to the regulator are independently reproduced, or the difference and its regulatory consequence are recorded.

testing.step: Test that the answer addressed the question asked
actions: Read each sampled question and the lodged answer side by side at the level of the numbered sub-question.
Mark any sub-question with no responsive answer, or answered by cross-reference to a document not attached.
Check whether a follow-up objection on the same point was subsequently received, which evidences a non-responsive answer.
Record non-responsive answers as exceptions with the resulting delay to disposition in days.
testing.done: every sampled sub-question is confirmed answered responsively, or the non-responsive answer and its delay are recorded.

testing.step: Test the clearance chain on the sampled responses
actions: Pull the clearance record for each sampled response and confirm the required clearances were given before the lodgement timestamp.
Confirm reserve answers carry Chief Actuary clearance and that anything conceding a wording or compliance point carries Regulatory Counsel clearance.
List responses lodged with clearance dated after lodgement or with no clearance at all as exceptions.
Check that any admission of a compliance failure was assessed for Art. 128 reporting before it was sent.
testing.done: every sampled response has clearances dated before lodgement, with reserve and concession clearances present.

testing.step: Trace amendments made by response back into the build inputs
actions: Identify sampled responses that amended filed wording, rates or reserve basis.
Confirm a new frozen package version and manifest were created and that the determination row and build inputs were updated to it.
Check the production configuration for the provision to confirm the amended, not the originally lodged, text was implemented.
Record any case where the superseded text reached production as a breach with the policies affected.
testing.done: every response-driven amendment is traced to a new frozen version and to the text actually in production.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the filing, the question number, what failed and the consequence to the filing timetable.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list (channel not swept, item not logged, deadline mis-recorded, owner capacity, clearance skipped, non-responsive answer, amendment not fed back) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where a filing was closed for non-response, agree with the Regulatory Affairs Manager how and when it will be refiled.
Carry every open exception into the next monthly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a tracker issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where relevant, a refiling plan.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: State the on-time response rate against the zero-missed-deadline threshold, split by channel and by answer owner.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper reference behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted and lodged none of the sampled responses and sits outside Regulatory Filing, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any filing closed for non-response to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper under REG-030.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the on-time rate by channel and owner, the conclusion and the committee reporting date.
